newsitem.title: UK: Asia draws nearly two mln tonnes of Euro gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia draws nearly two mln tonnes of Euro gas oil.

text.p: Asian demand for European gas oil was still strong two months after the arbitrage opened and upwards of two million tonnes has gone or is going east, traders said on Wednesday.
"The arb is open, there is a 50,000 tonne Black Sea cargo with early May dates that is likely to go to Singapore," said one trader.
Strong interest in Singapore and to a lesser degree in India has been supporting the European market by drawing away barrels from a fairly disinterested local market.
"It would be a very depressed market if we had not had this Asian draw," commented one broker.
"The big question is how long the arb will stay open, that's what everyone wants to know," said another dealer.

The spread between Russian prompt cif NWE gas oil against Singapore gas oil stands a touch over $35 a tonne, and although freight rates are strong, shipping brokers estimate a 60,000 tonne cargo should be able to secure a tanker to Singapore for $30 a tonne.

Factors that might hasten the closure of the arb window are tightening European supply which could inflate local prices. Traders said Russian gas oil becoming harder to find as agricultural demand for harvest fuel starts to kick in.
There were also signs that refiners were starting to look at maximising jet aviation fuel production over gas oil, which could also contribute to less supply and higher prices.
